annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Artificial intelligence: anticipating its impact on work to ensure a fair transition'
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Artificial intelligence: anticipating its impact on work to ensure a fair transition'
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 440/1
annotation.summary_en: EESC own-initiative opinion on how AI and robotics will affect work. It recommends ethical guidelines keeping humans in control of machines, algorithmic transparency, clarified liability for collaborative robot accidents under the Product Liability Directive, social dialogue, a European transition fund, an AI ethics observatory, and a debate on taxing robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: EU ethical guidelines on AI should ensure humans never become underlings of machines
Create a European observatory on AI ethics to monitor implementation
Clarify legal responsibility and health and safety risks of human-robot collaboration under the Product Liability Directive
Launch a debate on financing social protection and taxation in an economy with more robots
Establish a European transition fund and strengthen social dialogue and worker involvement
